newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine central bank considering hyrvnia regime.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine central bank considering hyrvnia regime.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank is considering two different currency regimes for its new hryvnia currency, the head of the bank said on Monday.

The central bank could peg the hryvnia in a narrow range against a single hard currency or link it more loosely to a currency or basket of currencies, National Bank Chairman Viktor Yushchenko told a news conference.
"We are considering either a narrow currency corridor for the hryvnia set against a hard currency, or a soft connection of the hryvnia to one or more foreign currencies," Yushchenko said.
The choice of currencies for the link was political rather than economic, he said.
The hryvnia, whose rate is fixed on the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange, has been unchanged at 1.76 to the dollar since it was introduced on September 2.
Yushchenko said previously a decision on the hryvnia regime would be settled once Ukraine receives a $1.5 billion currency stabilisation fund from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

A Fund mission is in Kiev to discuss a $2.5-3.0 billion Extended Fund Facility to succeed Ukraine's standby programme, which runs out at the beginning of next year. The stabilisation fund would be included in the facility.

"The central bank has already had primary discussions with the IMF over the chances of getting the currency stabilisation fund and the ideas behind which way to set the hryvnia's rate," Yushchenko said.
IMF experts supported the central bank's proposals for the hryvnia's rate, he added. --Natalya Zinets, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
